answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a bond locked for a cooling period, then slash it when independent, randomly assigned peers validate a signed interaction history and find fabricated identities reusing the same funding or behavior patterns. The shared evidence creates a ripple across the network: a sybil cluster cannot cheaply reset its reputation, even in a lagoon of new accounts. The crystal-clear cost is capital tied up for each identity, plus the risk of losing it when caught.
